title: FTSE Russell US indexes — December 2027 semi-annual reconstitution, implemented after the close of 2027-12-10 and effective at the open of 2027-12-13 (full cap-tier migration, reduced style and float scope)
source: EST: rule-derived by applying the owner's own published standing rule — already extracted from the primary and quoted verbatim in this calendar by the russell-reconstitution-2026-12-11 lane — to the December 2027 weekday calendar. THE RULE: FTSE Russell, "Russell US Equity Indexes" construction and methodology, v7.2, August 2026, section 4.2.3, "Reconstitution occurs on the fourth Friday in June and the second Friday in December", repeated at section 9.3.1, with Appendix F defining implementation as "the day changes are made after the close of the market and become effective at the open on the Monday following". THE ARITHMETIC: December 2027's Fridays are the 3rd, 10th, 17th, 24th and 31st, so the second is Friday 2027-12-10 and the Monday following is 2027-12-13. THE DERIVATION WAS TESTED, NOT ASSERTED — the same rule reproduces the tracked December 2026 instance exactly (December 2026's Fridays are the 4th, 11th, 18th and 25th; second = 2026-12-11, Monday following = 2026-12-14, which the July 2026 FAQ publishes independently as that quarter's Review Effective Date). It is further corroborated INSIDE this proposer's own research: FTSE Russell's July 2026 FAQ schedule table, re-fetched direct by this proposer 2026-09-09 (lseg.com dam, ftse-faq-document-russell-us-equity-2026.pdf, HTTP 200, 198,134 bytes, 19 content streams inflated in-session), publishes "Review Effective Date (open of) — 14 December 2026", and the Monday-after-the-implementation-Friday rule reproduces all four of its 2026 columns to the day. Filed estimate on the counts this calendar always records for this owner: a proposal is estimate by contract, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, the confirmed-tier prefixes in market-events-data.ts have no member for an index owner's own published schedule, and the FAQ's own schedule table carries "NOTE: Dates may be subject to change. Clients will be notified of any changes." No 2027 column has been published by the owner; this is a standing-rule derivation, not a read of a dated table. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED by the russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2027-12-31 initial research (2026-09-09). WHY IT MATTERS TO THE PROPOSER, AND WHY IT IS LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN SWEEP HABIT: this date IS the proposer's reset. The Russell US Style quarter-end capping test struck on the 2027-12-28 close reads a cohort whose capping factors were last set by the quarterly style capping review, and that review's effective open is the Monday after this implementation Friday — 2027-12-13. The proposer's entire base rate is the drift from that review's 2027-12-01 price date to the 2027-12-28 test, so a calendar that tracks the test and not the reset carries the conclusion without its cause. THE GAP IS EXACT: this calendar tracks russell-reconstitution- for 2026-12-11 and 2027-06-25 and stops; the December 2027 leg was simply missing. SCOPE, FROM THE OWNER'S OWN RULE AND NOT INFERRED — the December leg is deliberately NOT June's: ground rules v7.2 Appendix F's "Reconstitution updates" table (read and quoted by the russell-reconstitution-2026-12-11 lane) makes total market cap, nationality and total shares outstanding FULL in December, while float updates are "Applied with a 3% buffer", style probabilities cover only new additions and R1000/R2000/Microcap movements rather than the whole universe, and voting rights get "No adjustments or further research on existing members". That reduced scope is exactly why the proposer can still read its 18-session cut-off-to-test span as a price-drift window: the December recon's full leg is cap-tier migration between the R1000 and R2000, which does not touch a top-five mega-cap cohort, and its style and float legs — the ones that could move that cohort's weights — are the buffered, narrowed ones. A TAKING LANE SHOULD NOT RE-DERIVE TWO THINGS THE HARD WAY. First, the upstream chain is derivable from the same Appendix F and is deliberately NOT filed here, to keep one proposer from front-running a lane that would research them properly: rank day = last business day of October 2027 = Friday 2027-10-29, preliminary information = four weeks prior to implementation = Friday 2027-11-12, and this calendar already tracks that class as russell-recon-preliminary- and russell-recon-lockdown- for 2026 and mid-2027. Second, the corridor: 2027-12-10 sits two sessions before the 2027-12-13 effective open and eighteen before the proposer's own test, and this calendar's December 2027 entries within five days should be re-enumerated by the taking lane rather than copied from here. Impact medium mirrors the tracked 2026-12-11 instance — the flow is in the underlying names migrating between the R1000 and R2000, symbols is deliberately EMPTY for the same reason that entry gives (an ETF proxy would make the deterministic screen trip on small-cap beta, which carries no information about reconstitution scope), and kind `sector` matches the sibling market-structure flow entries because the enum has no index-flow member. Status estimate: it widens caution about the 2027-12-10 close and the 2027-12-13 open and licenses nothing.
